name: Bright Sparkle
description: The bright switch on at a low volume, where it gives the most, the treble up and the middle down: glassy chords and arpeggios.

name: Country Snap
description: The treble high, the middle scooped, and the bright switch on, for picked single notes and double stops that snap; the loudest of the clean ones, with its peaks just under where the power stage clips.

name: Cranked Combo
description: The volume near its top: the power stage clips, round and compressed, under a preamp that is still nearly clean. The loudest: its peaks are the power stage flat out.

name: Edge of Breakup
description: The volume past half way, where the power stage starts to round off the hardest notes: clean played softly, a little hair when dug into.

name: Normal Channel Jangle
description: The normal channel, two stages and some 8 dB less gain than the other, with the bright switch on: open strummed chords that stay clean however hard they are hit.

name: Pedal Platform
description: The low input, 6 dB down, with the volume under half and the stack flat: a clean stage for pedals in front that keeps their sound and its own headroom.

name: Studio Clean
description: The vibrato channel with the volume a quarter up and the stack near noon: the clean, wide sound the combo is known for, loud and with the power stage far from clipping. Put a cabinet after it, such as Boxed Twelves.

name: Warm Jazz
description: The normal channel with the treble down, the middle and the bass up: a round, dark clean for a neck pickup.
